entries.spiritual_meaning: The Infinite Divine Love itself — the Lord's own Esse, the absolute origin of all good and all being
entries.definition: As the supreme uncaused source from which all emanations proceed and to which all return, this figure corresponds to Divine Love in its infinite self-subsistence — the esse of the Lord that precedes and contains every derivative degree of good and truth.

variant_readings.reason_not_chosen: Too narrow; the Father encompasses both love and its wisdom as one infinite source, not just good as distinct from truth.

entries.notes: The text repeatedly states the Father is 'hidden and immeasurable' and 'established in himself alone' — corresponding precisely to Swedenborg's teaching that the Divine Esse is incomprehensible and self-subsistent. The Father's five limbs (mind, thought, insight, counsel, consideration) map to five essential faculties of the Divine itself.

entries.spiritual_meaning: The Lord as the Celestial Human — the Divine Rational proceeding into combat with the hells; the primordial celestial will united to the Divine
entries.definition: As the first being called forth to descend into the realm of darkness and wage war, this figure corresponds to the Lord's own Divine Human in its first proceeding — the celestial degree of the will that descends into the deepest states of temptation to confront and overcome evil from within.

variant_readings.reading: Primordial Divine Good descending into the natural mind
variant_readings.reason_not_chosen: Overlaps but is less precise; the First Man is specifically the Divine Human form that enters combat, not merely good in general.

entries.notes: The First Man is consistently presented as clothed in five garments (= five external truths) and descending voluntarily into the abyss. This mirrors Swedenborg's doctrine that the Lord assumed the human through successive natural states in order to combat the hells from within. The 'five sons' who remain behind in darkness after the First Man ascends correspond to the faculties of celestial perception still captive in the natural mind after the Lord's glorification.

entries.spiritual_meaning: The Lord's operative Divine Truth proceeding from Love — the Divine power that orders, judges, constructs, and sustains the whole spiritual world
entries.definition: As the being who rescues the First Man, constructs the universe from the bodies of defeated rulers, and establishes all order, the Living Spirit corresponds to the Lord's proceeding truth in its active, judicial, and architectural function — the power that creates spiritual order from what had been chaos.

variant_readings.reading: Divine Providence in its active operation
variant_readings.reason_not_chosen: Providence is one aspect of the Living Spirit's function; the primary correspondence is more comprehensive — the proceeding Divine Truth that both rescues, judges, and constructs.

entries.notes: The Living Spirit performs seven works, each corresponding to a complete operation of spiritual regeneration. The number seven here signifies holy fullness. The Living Spirit's 'five sons' correspond to the five structural powers that sustain the spiritual world — distinct from the First Man's five sons which are faculties of perception.

entries.spiritual_meaning: The Lord's mediating Divine Truth that proceeds into universal manifestation — the Divine principle that purifies wisdom from its admixture with falsity by displaying the Divine image
entries.definition: As the figure who displays his image to purify light from darkness, the Ambassador corresponds to the mediating function of Divine Truth — the proceeding that makes the Divine visible to all degrees of creation, drawing forth captive good by revealing the Divine likeness.

variant_readings.reading: Divine Providence proceeding into all things
variant_readings.reason_not_chosen: Providence is a function; the primary correspondence captures the Ambassador's distinctive method — making the Divine visible through its own image.

entries.notes: The Ambassador's distinctive act is displaying his 'image' — a correspondential term for the Divine Human form made perceptible to the understanding. When evil sees this image it lusts for it and generates counterfeits (Adam and Eve), teaching that the proprium cannot truly receive the Divine form but can only imitate it externally.

entries.spiritual_meaning: The Lord as Divine Wisdom made radiant — Divine Truth in its fullness of glory, proceeding to illuminate, liberate, and regenerate
entries.definition: As the figure who hunts after light and life through wisdom, who uproots evil perceptions and plants the tree of life, and who descends to Adam and Eve to give hope, Jesus the Splendour corresponds to Divine Truth in its saving, illuminating, and regenerative power — the Word made manifest.

variant_readings.reason_not_chosen: Captures one aspect but misses the saving and redemptive function that is equally central.

entries.notes: Jesus the Splendour occupies the fourth position in the hierarchy of 'fathers' and 'days,' corresponding to the fourth degree of illumination. His distinctive function is twofold: uprooting false perceptions (the bad fig-garden) and planting genuine ones (the tree of life). His 'twelve wisdoms' correspond to the twelve truths derived from good.

entries.spiritual_meaning: The Divine Truth proceeding from Love as the generative matrix of all spiritual life — the first operation of the Divine into created existence
entries.definition: As the first emanation from the Father who gives birth to the First Man and intercedes for his rescue, the Mother of Life corresponds to the Divine Wisdom in its generative and life-giving aspect — the proceeding Divine Truth that is the matrix or womb from which all derivative spiritual states are born.

variant_readings.reason_not_chosen: Narrower than the primary reading; the Mother is not just wisdom but specifically truth as the generative principle from which all spiritual life proceeds.

entries.notes: The Mother of Life is described as spending immeasurable time within the Father before being called forth — corresponding to the Swedenborgian teaching that Divine Truth exists in potential within Divine Love before proceeding. She is always paired with the Father of Life in the work of constructing the universe.

entries.spiritual_meaning: Pure uncorrupted wisdom — the affection of truth from good in its pristine, celestial innocence
entries.definition: As the figure who captivates the rulers through her beauty and gathers her own back to herself, the Virgin corresponds to pure truth united with celestial innocence — truth that is uncorrupted by any admixture of falsity, and whose spiritual beauty draws captive good toward liberation.
entries.notes: The Virgin's function of 'taking the heart of the rulers by her image' corresponds to how pure truth from good, by its inherent spiritual beauty, dispossesses evil of the good it holds captive. The extended parable of the free woman in her palace describes how celestial truth does not voluntarily expose itself to external states except out of love for the entrapped divine good.

entries.spiritual_meaning: The Lord's Divine Wisdom entering and operating within the human understanding — the interior illumination that regenerates the person
entries.definition: As the figure who descends into the individual body, binds the old man, loosens the soul's faculties from bondage, and constructs the new man, the Light Mind corresponds to Divine Wisdom as it flows into and transforms the individual human understanding — the actual operative power of regeneration within the person.
entries.notes: The Light Mind's entry into the body and its binding of the old man with five counsels directly corresponds to Swedenborg's teaching that the Lord's influx into the natural mind progressively subordinates the proprium. The Mind comes in secret, in love, with the Virgin of Light — that is, through interior affection and pure truth.

entries.spiritual_meaning: The sustaining Divine Truth that connects all degrees — the fully regenerated Divine Human form that upholds all spiritual order from the lowest to the highest
entries.definition: As the cosmic column bearing all things and connecting earth to heaven, the Pillar corresponds to the Lord's Divine Truth as it forms the ordered axis through which all influx descends and all purified good ascends — the vertical structure of discrete degrees made into a single form.

variant_readings.reason_not_chosen: The 'Perfect Man' aspect is part of the entry; the Pillar's primary function is sustaining and connecting, not just being the completed form.

entries.notes: The Pillar is identified both as a cosmic structure and as the Perfect Man — teaching that the fully regenerated human is itself the living connection between the lowest natural and the highest celestial. As one of the 'three great rocks,' it represents foundational truth that cannot be moved.

entries.spiritual_meaning: The proprium — the corporeal mind devoid of spiritual life; the self-derived will that fashions all forms of evil
entries.definition: As the female power that sculpts the world of darkness and gives strength to its king for war, Matter corresponds to the proprium — the inherited self-will that generates and sustains all forms of evil and falsity by fashioning them into organized external forms that imitate genuine life.
entries.notes: Matter is consistently called 'the thought of death' — the proprium conceived not as inert substance but as an active intention toward spiritual death. She is the 'mother' of all evil affections, corresponding to Swedenborg's teaching that the proprium is the womb from which all particular evils are born.

natural_variants: King of the realms of Darkness
entries.spiritual_meaning: The ruling principle of self-love — the sovereign evil that governs all states of falsity from evil
entries.definition: As the supreme ruler of the five dark worlds who consolidates all evil under himself for war against the light, this figure corresponds to the ruling love of self in its most organized and dominant form — the love of dominion from self that is the head of all hells.
entries.notes: The five shapes upon the King (lion, demon, eagle, dragon, fish) correspond to five genera of evil operating through him. His qualities — hardness, magic, limited perception — describe how ruling self-love is impervious to truth, operates through persuasive falsity, and can only perceive what is immediately present (i.e., has no foresight).

entries.spiritual_meaning: The fully realized Divine Human form — the completed Grand Man of all regenerated good and truth gathered into final unity
entries.definition: As the ultimate form into which all purified life is gathered and sculpted at the end, the Last Statue corresponds to the completed universal human — the Grand Man of heaven in its final perfection, composed of every good and truth that has been liberated from its captivity in the natural world.
entries.notes: The Last Statue teaching parallels Swedenborg's Grand Man (Maximus Homo) — the complete form of heaven constituted from all angelic societies. Its being 'sculpted' from what is gathered teaches that the collective form of heaven is not automatic but requires active divine ordering.

entries.spiritual_meaning: The Lord's calling forth of divine truth — the active influx of truth from the Divine into the human will
entries.definition: As the voice sent from above to the captive First Man, the summons corresponds to the active proceeding of truth from the Lord — the Divine call that penetrates into the deepest states of captivity and initiates the process of liberation and regeneration.
entries.notes: The summons and the obedience together form a conjugial pair — the father-principle and mother-principle of spiritual communication. The summons is always active and descending; the obedience is always receptive and ascending.

entries.spiritual_meaning: The will's willing reception of divine truth — the responsive ascent of good toward the Lord's calling
entries.definition: As the answer that ascends from the First Man back to the Living Spirit, the obedience corresponds to the human will's free response to divine truth — the reception and acknowledgment that completes the circuit of influx and makes regeneration possible.
entries.notes: The obedience is compared to a letter written from the battlefield — the interior communication of all temptation-states back to the Divine. This teaching corresponds to Swedenborg's doctrine that the Lord perceives all states of the person in temptation through the medium of the person's own responsive acknowledgment.

entries.spiritual_meaning: Divine wisdom — truth proceeding from love that illuminates the understanding
entries.opposite_sense: When stolen or counterfeited by evil: falsified truth, or truth appropriated to self
entries.definition: As the universal medium of vision and knowledge, light corresponds to divine wisdom and truth — that which proceeds from the Lord's love and enables the understanding to perceive spiritual realities. Light is the form that love takes when it enters the intellect.

variant_readings.reason_not_chosen: Synonymous in many contexts but 'wisdom' better captures the full scope — light is not merely truth as proposition but truth as interior perception.

entries.notes: The most fundamental correspondence in the entire text. 'Light' pervades every chapter and is consistently rendered as wisdom or truth from the Divine. The five 'light elements' are wisdom differentiated into its five constituent faculties.

entries.spiritual_meaning: Falsity from evil — the absence and opposition of divine wisdom; spiritual ignorance proceeding from self-love
entries.definition: As the absence and enemy of light, darkness corresponds to falsity proceeding from evil — not mere ignorance but the active privation and corruption of truth that flows from self-love and constitutes the essential nature of all hells.
entries.notes: Darkness is not merely passive absence but active opposition — it 'stirs itself,' 'rises up,' and 'makes war.' This corresponds to Swedenborg's teaching that falsity from evil is not mere privation but a living, active force proceeding from the hells.

entries.spiritual_meaning: Divine Love — celestial love that is the inmost life of all spiritual reality
entries.definition: As the element that is 'above them all' and constitutes the inmost garment of the First Man, living fire corresponds to Divine Love — the supreme animating principle from which all other spiritual faculties derive their life.
entries.notes: Living fire is present in eight places according to the text — eight states of spiritual order. It is the first and last garment of the First Man, teaching that divine love is both the inmost origin and the ultimate consummation of all the Lord's work. The living fire 'withers the tumescence of the enemy' — love alone has power to collapse the inflation of self-love.

entries.spiritual_meaning: Self-love — the consuming infernal love that burns with the desire to dominate and possess
entries.definition: As the element belonging to the world of fire whose king is lion-faced, dark fire corresponds to self-love — the love of dominating others from oneself that is the ruling evil of the hells and the consuming passion that destroys all genuine spiritual life.
entries.notes: Dark fire is paired with 'lust' as the father and mother of all evil generation. The great fire at the end of the world that dissolves all things corresponds to the final judgment through divine love consuming what is false.

entries.spiritual_meaning: Living truth — truth that purifies, regenerates, and carries spiritual life
entries.definition: As the element in which the First Man dwells (in his ship) and which purifies and regenerates, living water corresponds to truth that carries genuine spiritual life — truth proceeding from good that cleanses the understanding and sustains the soul.
entries.notes: The 'ship of living waters' is consistently identified with the moon and with the First Man's dwelling — teaching that truth as doctrine is the containing form through which celestial good operates in the spiritual degree.

entries.spiritual_meaning: Falsity itself — corrupted truth; the pervasive medium through which evil is communicated and spread
entries.definition: As the dark element whose king is fish-faced and whose taste is deceptive sweetness, dark water corresponds to falsity in its fluid, pervasive form — corrupted truth that flows through all states of the mind, carrying evil influence wherever it goes.
entries.notes: The dark water vessels are the first to be discharged from the heavens — corresponding to the teaching that falsities of the understanding are addressed before the deeper evils of the will in regeneration.

entries.spiritual_meaning: The living influx of the spirit — the active flow of understanding into the mind from the Divine
entries.definition: As the element that blows and moves actively, living wind corresponds to the influx of spiritual understanding — the breath of the Divine spirit that flows into the rational faculty and gives it the power of active thought.

variant_readings.reason_not_chosen: Valid but narrower; the living wind is the influx itself rather than the truth it carries.

entries.notes: Wind as one of the three garments of the Living Spirit corresponds to the doctrine of understanding — the external form of truth operating in the rational plane.

entries.spiritual_meaning: False persuasion — vain reasoning; the force of argument from falsity
entries.definition: As the dark element whose king is eagle-faced and whose taste is 'sharp,' dark wind corresponds to false persuasion — the force of reasoning from falsity that cuts and divides, creating the appearance of intellectual power while serving evil ends.
entries.notes: The eagle-faced quality of the wind-king corresponds to predatory intellectual sight — rationality that seizes and devours rather than illuminates.

entries.spiritual_meaning: Obscurity of understanding — dense falsity arising from evil that darkens the intellect
entries.definition: As the element that obscures vision and rises from burning, smoke corresponds to the obscurity of understanding that arises when the mind's intellectual faculty is dominated by self-love — dense falsity that clouds all perception.
entries.notes: The world of Smoke is consistently identified with the 'mind' (nous) — but in its perverted form, the intellectual faculty given over to evil. Its king came up 'from the depth of darkness' as the first to make war, teaching that intellectual pride proceeding from self-love is the origin of all spiritual assault.

entries.spiritual_meaning: The living sphere of spiritual perception — the rational atmosphere in which the mind breathes and perceives truth
entries.definition: As the element that all flesh lives upon by breathing, the living air corresponds to the sphere of spiritual perception — the rational atmosphere proceeding from the Divine in which the understanding subsists and through which it perceives all spiritual realities.
entries.notes: The living air is unique among the five elements: it alone was not wounded in the first combat. This corresponds to the teaching that the rational sphere of spiritual life — the inmost level of understanding closest to the celestial — cannot be penetrated by falsity from evil. It becomes the 'spirit of life' for the other four, teaching that the rational degree sustains all lower faculties.

entries.spiritual_meaning: Semblance of celestial good — the external form that counterfeits heavenly love; or, positively, celestial good itself
entries.opposite_sense: When attributed to the King of Darkness: the counterfeit of celestial good used as a disguise for evil
entries.definition: As the most precious metal associated with the body of the King of Smoke, gold corresponds to the appearance of celestial good — which, when appropriated by evil, becomes the most dangerous form of counterfeit: evil disguised as the highest good.
entries.notes: Gold belonging to the rulers of Smoke (perverted intellect) signifies how self-love clothes itself in the appearance of celestial good. This is the deepest deception — evil that presents itself not merely as natural good but as divine love itself.

entries.spiritual_meaning: Spiritual truth — or, when belonging to darkness, falsified truth
entries.opposite_sense: When attributed to the realm of water/darkness: truth perverted to serve evil ends
entries.definition: As the metal associated with the rulers of the world of Water, silver corresponds to truth in its spiritual form — which, when corrupted, becomes falsified truth that retains the appearance of truth while serving falsehood.
entries.notes: Silver belongs to the water-world, whose king is fish-faced. The conjunction of silver with deceptive sweetness teaches that falsified truth is especially dangerous because it tastes pleasant — it satisfies the understanding's desire for truth while actually confirming falsity.

entries.spiritual_meaning: Perverted natural good — natural good turned to serve self-love
entries.definition: As the metal associated with the rulers of the world of Fire, copper corresponds to natural good that has been perverted — external acts of good performed not from charity but from the love of dominion.
entries.notes: Copper belongs to the fire-world (self-love). Swedenborg identifies copper with natural good; here in the dark sense it signifies natural good made to serve infernal ends.

entries.spiritual_meaning: Hardened natural truth — truth in its most unyielding and resistant form; or natural truth applied with severity
entries.opposite_sense: When belonging to darkness: hardened natural falsity impervious to correction
entries.definition: As the hardest common metal and the body of the wind-world rulers, iron corresponds to natural truth in its most rigid form — which, when perverted, becomes hardened falsity that resists all penetration by genuine truth.
entries.notes: Iron's hardness is emphasized repeatedly in describing the King of Darkness's impenetrability. In its positive sense, iron implements are used to work the earth — corresponding to natural truths applied to reform the natural mind.

entries.spiritual_meaning: The densest, basest falsity — the heaviest and most external form of perverted truth
entries.definition: As the heaviest metal assigned to the world of pure Darkness, lead corresponds to the densest and most external form of falsity — falsity so heavy with evil that it sinks to the lowest possible state.
entries.notes: Lead belongs to the dragon-ruled world of pure Darkness, the lowest of all infernal states. Its extreme density corresponds to falsity so deeply embedded in evil that it constitutes the very substance of the lowest hell.

entries.spiritual_meaning: A discrete state of spiritual life — a heavenly degree or society within the Lord's kingdom
entries.opposite_sense: When belonging to darkness: an infernal state or hellish condition
entries.definition: As the cosmic realm in which divine beings dwell, an aeon corresponds to a discrete state or degree of spiritual life — each aeon being a distinct condition of reception of the Divine, from the most celestial to the most natural.
entries.notes: The text uses 'aeon' for both positive and negative states — 'aeons of light' and by implication 'aeons of darkness.' The 'new aeon' constructed by the Great Builder corresponds to the new heaven established after the last judgment.

entries.spiritual_meaning: A containing form or vessel — a doctrinal structure that carries and conveys divine good or truth through successive states
entries.opposite_sense: When dark: a containing form emptied of life
entries.definition: As the vessel that carries beings across the cosmic sea, a ship corresponds to a doctrinal form or vessel of reception — the organized structure of truth that carries the mind's affections and understandings from one state to another.
entries.notes: The two primary ships — of living fire (sun/day) and living waters (moon/night) — correspond to the two fundamental doctrinal vessels: the doctrine of celestial love and the doctrine of spiritual truth. The sun's ship never wanes while the moon's does, teaching that the vessel of love is perpetually full while the vessel of faith fluctuates.

entries.spiritual_meaning: A discrete degree of heavenly order — a structural separation between interior and exterior states of the mind
entries.definition: As the solid boundary dividing upper from lower cosmic regions, a firmament corresponds to a discrete degree of spiritual order — the structural boundary that separates one level of the mind from the next, preventing improper mixing while allowing ordered influx.
entries.notes: The 'ten firmaments' correspond to the ten ascending degrees of heavenly consciousness. Doors opening in the firmaments correspond to communications between discrete degrees being opened by Divine influx.

entries.spiritual_meaning: The providential cycle of spiritual reformation — the revolving order of knowledges and states through which the mind is progressively purified
entries.definition: As the revolving sphere that carries the stars and zodiac, the wheel corresponds to the ordered cycle of Divine Providence — the revolving arrangement of spiritual knowledges and states that serves as both a purifying mechanism and a restraint upon evil.
entries.notes: The wheel is described as having no root in the earth but gaining authority through the fall of evil upon it — teaching that the cycle of natural knowledges has no inherent spiritual power but gained dominion over the proprium only because evil contaminated it during the fall.

entries.spiritual_meaning: Divine restraint upon evil — the ordering power that confines falsity and evil within limits so they cannot spread
entries.opposite_sense: When imposed by evil: the captivity and bondage in which the proprium holds the living soul
entries.definition: As the chain that holds the rulers in their appointed places, a bond corresponds to the divine ordering that restrains evil within fixed limits — preventing the hells from exceeding their appointed bounds and destroying spiritual freedom.
entries.notes: The 'lump' — the final bond — is the ultimate consolidated mass of evil from which there is no liberation. It corresponds to the eternal state of hell where evil is permanently sealed.

entries.spiritual_meaning: A governing principle of spiritual authority — a seat of divine judgment and governance over a particular domain
entries.opposite_sense: When belonging to darkness: a seat of evil power
entries.definition: As the seat upon which a ruler exercises authority, a throne corresponds to a governing principle — the organized authority through which the Divine or its opposite exercises dominion over a particular region of the spiritual world.
entries.notes: Eighteen thrones are named — nine in the interior heavens and nine in the intermediate sphere — teaching that divine governance operates through corresponding degrees in both the celestial kingdom and the world of spirits.

entries.spiritual_meaning: The natural mind — the ground of reception upon which spiritual life is built; or the celestial good in which the Divine dwells
entries.opposite_sense: When qualified as 'of Darkness': the natural mind given over to falsity from evil
entries.definition: As the ground that receives seed and produces growth, the earth corresponds to the natural mind as receptive ground — the plane of consciousness where spiritual truths are implanted and either grow into good works or are choked by evil.
entries.notes: The 'three earths' correspond to three degrees of the natural mind. The 'light-earth' of the Father is the infinite ground of divine good. The 'earth of Darkness' is the natural mind wholly given over to evil. The text consistently teaches that these earths are 'conjoined' — the natural mind is a unified structure with discrete levels.

entries.spiritual_meaning: An elevated state of love or perception — or, in the negative sense, a state of self-exaltation in falsity
entries.opposite_sense: When belonging to darkness: prideful self-exaltation; mountains of Darkness = states of self-exaltation in falsity
entries.definition: As elevated terrain rising above the plain, mountains correspond to elevated states of the will — either genuine states of celestial love rising toward the Divine, or the inflated pride of self-love exalting itself above its proper degree.
entries.notes: The 'four mountains' surrounding the earth correspond to four elevated states of celestial good that enclose and protect the natural mind. Mountains in the realm of darkness correspond to pride — the 'black mountain near the sunrise' signifies self-intelligence persisting even near the source of illumination.

entries.spiritual_meaning: A containing form of reception — a doctrinal or structural form that holds and conveys spiritual substance
entries.opposite_sense: When dark: a containing form of evil — a structure that holds falsity or perverted love
entries.definition: As a container that holds and preserves its contents, a vessel corresponds to a containing form — the organized doctrinal or mental structure through which spiritual substance (whether good or evil) is received, preserved, and conveyed.
entries.notes: The 'three vessels' that surround the universe correspond to containing forms of corrupted truth, falsity, and infernal desire. Their being 'discharged' corresponds to the process of vastation — evils first brought into conscious awareness and then expelled.

entries.spiritual_meaning: A protective boundary of truth — the outermost enclosure that separates and protects the regenerated mind from external evil
entries.definition: As the outermost enclosure of a city or building, a wall corresponds to the protective boundary of truth — the outermost doctrinal truths that surround and defend the interior life from invasion by falsity from evil.
entries.notes: The 'wall of great fire' that surrounds the entire building corresponds to the ultimate boundary of divine love that encloses all creation — within which evil is confined and from which the aeons of light are protected.

entries.spiritual_meaning: A passage of communication between degrees — the opening through which influx passes from one state of the mind to another
entries.definition: As an opening that permits or prevents passage, a gate corresponds to the means of communication between discrete spiritual degrees — the openings through which divine influx enters or through which the soul passes from one state to another.
entries.notes: Gates opening before influx and closing behind it corresponds to the teaching that each discrete degree receives the Divine proceeding and then seals itself — influx moves only in one direction through discrete degrees.

entries.spiritual_meaning: The ruling love — the governing principle of the whole spiritual life; or, inmost wisdom
entries.definition: As the part of the body from which all other members depend and which contains the organs of highest perception, the head corresponds to the ruling love — the single governing affection from which all other faculties of the spiritual life proceed and upon which they all depend.
entries.notes: The text explicitly teaches the correspondence: 'as the root of all limbs hang upon the head, so if one limb be cut off while the head exists, there is hope; but if the head be cut off, the entire body dies.' This directly parallels Swedenborg's teaching about the ruling love.

entries.spiritual_meaning: The will — the seat of love and the innermost center of spiritual life
entries.definition: As the organ that circulates life-giving blood through the body, the heart corresponds to the will — the central faculty of love from which all spiritual life flows and which governs the direction and quality of the whole person's existence.
entries.notes: The heart is described as 'the king' to whom all five senses report — corresponding to the will as the central governing faculty that receives input from all perceptive functions. The heart being likened to the King of Honour who governs the seven firmaments teaches that the will governs all rational degrees.

entries.spiritual_meaning: Intellectual sight — the faculty of the understanding by which spiritual truth is perceived
entries.definition: As the organ that receives light and forms images, the eye corresponds to intellectual sight — the understanding's capacity to perceive truth, discern forms, and apprehend spiritual realities through the light of divine wisdom.
entries.notes: The two eyes are likened to the two ships of light (sun and moon) — the containing forms of love and truth by which the understanding perceives. The pupil that perceives by day but not by night teaches that intellectual sight operates only in states of spiritual illumination.

entries.spiritual_meaning: Obedient reception — the faculty by which divine truth is heard and received into the understanding
entries.definition: As the organ that receives sound, the ear corresponds to the faculty of obedient reception — the understanding's capacity to hear and receive truth communicated from the Divine or from others.
entries.notes: The ear's repository that preserves sound 'for a thousand days' corresponds to the memory's preservation of heard truths through a complete state of spiritual development.

entries.spiritual_meaning: Perception rooted in divine wisdom — a living system of understanding that grows from good and produces genuine spiritual works
entries.definition: As a living organism that grows from its root, draws nourishment from the earth, and produces fruit, the good tree corresponds to a perception rooted in divine wisdom — an organized system of understanding that draws life from the Lord's love and produces genuine works of charity.
entries.notes: The good tree has five limbs corresponding to five ascending faculties (consideration, counsel, insight, thought, mind) — teaching that genuine perception is organized in discrete ascending degrees from outermost reception to inmost willing.

entries.spiritual_meaning: Perception rooted in self-intelligence — a system of understanding that grows from evil and produces only false and harmful works
entries.definition: As a tree that grows from corrupted soil and produces inedible or poisonous fruit, the bad tree corresponds to perception rooted in self-intelligence — understanding organized not from divine influx but from the proprium, producing works that are spiritually harmful.
entries.notes: The bad tree has the same five-limb structure as the good tree but inverted — teaching that self-intelligence mimics the structure of genuine wisdom but reverses its direction: from the rule of spiritual death to the ultimate mass of consolidated evil.

entries.spiritual_meaning: Good works — the deeds of charity that flow from genuine perception of truth united with love
entries.definition: As the product of a tree's growth that provides nourishment, good fruit corresponds to the works of charity — the deeds and effects that proceed from a mind rooted in divine wisdom and animated by genuine love of the neighbor.
entries.notes: The teaching that good fruit cannot arise from the bad tree directly parallels the Lord's teaching in Matthew 7:18.

entries.spiritual_meaning: Evil works — deeds proceeding from self-love and falsity that harm spiritual life
entries.definition: As the inedible or poisonous product of a corrupted tree, bad fruit corresponds to evil works — the deeds and their effects that proceed from self-intelligence and self-love, which damage both the doer and others.
entries.notes: The text teaches that evil 'spent a long time in the fruits before it sculpted the demons' — evil works precede and eventually give rise to organized evil affections.

entries.spiritual_meaning: External truth clothing interior good — the outermost layer of truth that protects, accommodates, and makes the interior accessible
entries.opposite_sense: When torn or ragged: devastated and degraded truths stripped of their life
entries.definition: As the outermost covering of the body that protects and presents the person, garments correspond to external truths — the outermost doctrinal coverings that clothe interior good, protect it from profanation, and accommodate it for reception by others.
entries.notes: The five garments of the First Man are five successive layers of external truth by which the Divine accommodated itself for combat with the hells. The three garments of the Living Spirit (wind, fire, water) correspond to the three doctrinal forms through which Providence operates. 'Rags' signify degraded truths still containing some life.

entries.spiritual_meaning: The Lord as Divine Love — or Divine Truth proceeding from love as the source of all spiritual illumination
entries.definition: As the source of all light and warmth in the natural world, the sun corresponds to the Lord as Divine Love and Wisdom — the one source from which all spiritual illumination and warmth of charity proceed into the created universe.

variant_readings.reason_not_chosen: The sun signifies divine love as ruling good in some contexts and divine wisdom/truth in others; the primary correspondence encompasses both as the Lord's proceeding.

entries.notes: The sun's ship 'never wanes' while the moon's does — teaching that the Lord's love is perpetually full and constant while faith fluctuates. Seven good things the sun does daily correspond to seven complete operations of divine truth in the regenerating mind.

entries.spiritual_meaning: Faith from natural truth — divine truth as it operates in states of spiritual obscurity; the containing form of truth
entries.definition: As the lesser light that shines by reflected light in the night, the moon corresponds to faith — truth received from the Lord that illuminates the understanding even in states of spiritual obscurity, though with reflected rather than direct light.
entries.notes: The moon waxes and wanes while the sun does not — teaching that faith fluctuates while love remains constant. The moon is always paired with 'living waters' (truth), distinguishing it from the sun's 'living fire' (love).

entries.spiritual_meaning: Knowledge of good and truth — particular items of spiritual knowledge that illuminate like individual points of light
entries.definition: As individual points of light in the heavens, stars correspond to particular knowledges of good and truth — the discrete items of spiritual understanding that together constitute the complete body of knowledge through which the mind is illuminated.
entries.notes: Stars are bound on the revolving wheel — teaching that knowledges of spiritual truth are organized within the cyclical order of Providence. The stars' authority over the flesh came through the fall — not from inherent power but from evil contaminating the cycle of natural knowledge.

entries.spiritual_meaning: The general mass of natural knowledge — the vast aggregate of sensory and factual knowledge in the outermost memory
entries.definition: As the vast body of water that receives all rivers and upon which ships sail, the sea corresponds to the general mass of natural knowledge in the external memory — the aggregate of sensory experience and factual knowing upon which doctrinal systems navigate.
entries.notes: The salty inner sea signifies natural knowledge adulterated by the residue of evil — corresponding to how the outermost memory inevitably carries traces of corruption. The sea giant formed within the sea corresponds to the monstrous composite selfhood that consolidates within this mass of natural knowledge.

entries.spiritual_meaning: A stream of truth — a particular flowing current of understanding proceeding from a higher source
entries.definition: As a flowing body of water that proceeds from a source and nourishes the land through which it passes, a river corresponds to a stream of truth — a particular flow of understanding that proceeds from a higher spiritual source and nourishes the mind through which it passes.
entries.notes: The Tigris is described as merely one river among thousands of rivers from unrevealed secrets — teaching that any particular natural-plane stream of truth is only a minute fraction of the immense flow of truth from the Divine.

entries.spiritual_meaning: A precious interior truth of faith — a truth of great spiritual value formed through suffering and refinement
entries.definition: As a precious object formed within a living creature under adverse conditions, a pearl corresponds to an interior truth of faith — a spiritual understanding of great value that is refined and perfected through the process of temptation.
entries.notes: The First Man being brought up 'like a pearl from the sea' teaches that the celestial state of innocence is rescued from the overwhelming mass of natural knowledge as a truth of supreme value is drawn from the depths.

entries.spiritual_meaning: Encompassing doctrine — the organized teaching of truth that captures and draws forth spiritual life from its captivity in falsity
entries.opposite_sense: When belonging to evil: the persuasive means by which self-love ensnares spiritual life
entries.definition: As an implement that captures what is within a body of water, a net corresponds to encompassing doctrine — the organized system of truth through which the Divine draws forth captive good and truth from the general mass of natural knowledge.
entries.notes: Each of the four divine hunters uses a distinct net — teaching that each degree of divine operation employs its own form of encompassing doctrine suited to the plane on which it operates.

entries.spiritual_meaning: Obscured truth — truth in its natural, accommodated form; truth veiled for reception by lower states
entries.definition: As a formation that carries water between heaven and earth while obscuring the sun, a cloud corresponds to truth in its natural, obscured form — divine truth veiled and accommodated so that it can descend into lower states of the mind for reception.
entries.notes: The four types of clouds (fire, water, wind, light) correspond to four modes of obscured truth ascending from the four elements toward purification. Each type releases its ruling evil upon ascent, corresponding to how truths rising toward purity trigger the expulsion of embedded falsities.

entries.spiritual_meaning: Spiritual reformation — the progressive separation of good from evil and truth from falsity within the regenerating mind
entries.definition: As the process of removing impurities from a substance, purification corresponds to the spiritual process by which good is progressively separated from evil and truth from falsity — the essential work of regeneration that transforms the mixed state of the natural mind into ordered heavenly life.
entries.notes: The entire text presents purification as the central purpose of the created order — the universe itself is a mechanism designed for the progressive separation and purification of wisdom from its admixture with falsity.

entries.spiritual_meaning: Spiritual temptation — the combat between good and evil, truth and falsity, within the regenerating mind
entries.definition: As armed conflict between opposing forces, war corresponds to spiritual temptation — the intense interior combat in which the forces of divine good and truth contend against the forces of evil and falsity for possession of the person's will and understanding.
entries.notes: Five wars correspond to five degrees of spiritual combat — each more interior than the last, culminating in the work of providence that gathers all into the final form.

entries.spiritual_meaning: Elevation toward celestial states — the progressive interiorization of the mind from natural to spiritual to celestial degrees
entries.definition: As upward movement from lower to higher ground, ascent corresponds to the elevation of the mind toward more interior states — the progressive movement from natural understanding through spiritual perception to celestial wisdom.
entries.notes: The ascent of the elements through successive degrees — light to fire to water to wind to air — corresponds to the gathering of goods and truths from outmost to inmost.

entries.spiritual_meaning: Proceeding into lower states — the accommodation of divine influx through successive degrees into the natural mind
entries.opposite_sense: When evil descends: the fall of evil from interior concealment into the natural mind where it can be confronted
entries.definition: As downward movement from higher to lower ground, descent corresponds to the proceeding of divine influx into lower degrees — the accommodation by which the infinite makes itself receivable in the finite, or the exposure of hidden evil into conscious awareness.
entries.notes: The First Man's descent and the subsequent discharging of the three vessels both describe descent — but of opposite kinds: divine descent to rescue, and the descent of evil into conscious awareness for removal. Both are essential to regeneration.

entries.spiritual_meaning: The giving of determinate spiritual form — the active shaping of interior states into organized structures whether of good or evil
entries.definition: As the act of giving form to raw material, sculpting corresponds to the process of giving determinate spiritual form — whether the Divine ordering goods and truths into heavenly structures, or the proprium fashioning evil affections into organized systems of falsity.
entries.notes: Both the Divine and Matter 'sculpt' — teaching that the same process of giving form operates in opposite directions: the Divine forms goods and truths into heavenly order, while the proprium forms evils and falsities into organized hells.

entries.spiritual_meaning: Spiritual life — the continuous reception of love and wisdom from the Lord into the will and understanding
entries.definition: As the animating principle that distinguishes living beings from dead matter, life corresponds to spiritual life — the state of receiving influx of love and wisdom from the Lord, which alone constitutes genuine existence.
entries.notes: The text consistently pairs 'life' with 'light' as the two aspects of what the Divine hunters seek to recover — corresponding to Swedenborg's pairing of good (life) and truth (light) as the twofold proceeding from the Lord.

entries.spiritual_meaning: Spiritual death — the state of complete separation from the Lord's influx; the condition of the proprium when cut off from all divine life
entries.definition: As the cessation of biological life, death corresponds to spiritual death — the state in which the will and understanding are wholly cut off from the Lord's influx of love and wisdom, subsisting only in the reactive energies of self-love.
entries.notes: Two deaths are distinguished: the first is temporal (lasting until purification is complete) and the second is eternal. This maps precisely to Swedenborg's distinction between vastation (temporary) and the second death (permanent spiritual death).

entries.spiritual_meaning: Interior peace — the state of rest and conjunction that comes when goods and truths are conjoined and all conflict in the mind ceases
entries.definition: As the cessation of conflict and the presence of harmony, peace corresponds to the interior spiritual state in which goods and truths are perfectly conjoined and there is no opposition between the will and the understanding — the deepest rest that comes from conjunction with the Divine.
entries.notes: The text teaches that the peace given in descent is the same as the peace in ascent — divine conjunction is not interrupted by temptation but passes through it unbroken. This is a key Swedenborgian principle.

entries.spiritual_meaning: Divine Love itself — the infinite esse of the Lord from which all good proceeds
entries.definition: As the deepest affection uniting persons, love corresponds to the very esse of the Divine — the infinite good from which all derivative goods proceed and which constitutes the life of all that lives.
entries.notes: The text defines love as 'the Father' — that is, the Divine itself. 'Love is the Father of Greatness who dwells in his glorious land. The entirety of the divine has been revealed therein.' This directly parallels Swedenborg's identification of Divine Love with the Lord's own esse.

entries.spiritual_meaning: The primal spiritual death — the consuming hatred of all good that arises from self-love; the essential nature of evil
entries.definition: As the opposite of love, hate corresponds to the essential nature of evil — the consuming desire to destroy what is not one's own, arising from self-love and constituting the very life of all hells.
entries.notes: Hate is defined as 'the first death that welled up' — the primordial spiritual death that manifests the realm of falsity. Its essential quality is envy — 'the hatred of all life and good that belongs to another.' This corresponds precisely to Swedenborg's teaching that the essential nature of evil is the lust to appropriate what belongs to the Divine.

entries.spiritual_meaning: Pristine wisdom — truth that has never been contaminated by falsity or conjunction with evil
entries.definition: As the state of never having been conjoined with another, virginity corresponds to pristine wisdom — truth that has never tasted spiritual death, never been defiled by conjunction with falsity, and retains its original purity from the Divine.
entries.notes: Contrasted with 'continent' (= restored wisdom that was defiled but has been purified). This distinction parallels Swedenborg's distinction between celestial innocence (never fallen) and spiritual innocence (restored through regeneration).

entries.spiritual_meaning: Restored wisdom — truth that was contaminated by falsity but has been purified and returned to holiness
entries.definition: As the state of having renounced what one formerly indulged, continence corresponds to restored wisdom — truth that descended into mixture with falsity, was defiled, but has been purified through the process of regeneration and restored to its proper holy state.
entries.notes: The text defines this precisely: 'it tasted of the lust; but afterwards was cleansed from it and became a holy one.' This corresponds to the Swedenborgian 'spiritual' degree — truth that has been through temptation and emerged purified.

entries.spiritual_meaning: Conjunction and distinction — the quality of duality as in will and understanding, good and truth, love and wisdom
entries.definition: Two signifies the quality of conjunction-in-distinction, particularly the fundamental duality of will and understanding, good and truth, love and wisdom — the two aspects of every spiritual reality that must be united for completeness.
entries.notes: Two essences (light and darkness), two ships (sun and moon), two deaths, two sons of the First Man, two eyes of the body — in every case, two signifies a fundamental duality that defines the structure of reality. The 'two per world' describes the masculine/feminine (= intellectual/volitional) polarity within each degree.

entries.spiritual_meaning: Fullness as to degrees — completeness in the vertical dimension of discrete degrees (celestial, spiritual, natural)
entries.definition: Three signifies fullness as to discrete degrees — the complete vertical structure of successive planes through which the Divine proceeds and through which all spiritual reality is organized: the celestial, the spiritual, and the natural.
entries.notes: Three earths, three vessels, three garments, three rocks, three emanations from each father, three seasons, three days, three deaths, three wars — the number three pervades the text's architecture. Every triad represents the same reality: the threefold structure of discrete degrees through which all spiritual substance passes.

entries.spiritual_meaning: Fullness of reception in all directions — completeness of conjunction with the Divine in every quarter of spiritual existence
entries.definition: Four signifies fullness of reception in all directions — the complete spatial extent of spiritual reception, like the four cardinal points or four walls that enclose and protect from every side.
entries.notes: Four days, four nights, four hunters, four advents, four mountains, four walls, four climes — four consistently signifies the complete quadrant-structure of spiritual reception. The four are always 'distributed three by three before his face' when combined with twelve, showing the relationship between four (reception) and twelve (completeness).

entries.spiritual_meaning: Fullness as to manifestation — the complete set of spiritual faculties through which interior reality is expressed and perceived in the outermost degree
entries.definition: Five signifies fullness as to manifestation in the sensory and natural degree — the complete complement of faculties (perception, thought, insight, counsel, consideration) by which the spiritual is made present in the natural, and by which the natural perceives the spiritual.
entries.notes: The number five is the most architecturally significant number in the entire corpus. Five elements, five worlds, five garments, five sons, five fathers, five trees, five fleshes, five senses, five faculties of the mind, five wars, five releases, five watches, five camps — everything in this text is organized in fives. The five always correspond to the complete set of faculties by which spiritual reality is made manifest and perceived at a given degree.

entries.spiritual_meaning: Holy fullness — completeness of a spiritual state or process from beginning to end
entries.definition: Seven signifies what is holy and complete — the fullness of a spiritual state or operation when it has passed through all its phases and reached its divine conclusion. It represents the sanctification of what six (labor) has prepared.
entries.notes: Seven works of the Living Spirit, seven firmaments, seven hostels for rebels, seven ditches, seven rulers in each bodily world, seven good things the sun does, seven evil things the night does — seven consistently signifies the complete cycle of a spiritual process. The seventh firmament where the King of Honour dwells is the inmost rational degree.

entries.spiritual_meaning: Fullness of remains — all truths and goods stored inwardly by the Lord for use in regeneration
entries.definition: Ten signifies the fullness of remains — all the goods and truths that the Lord stores within the interior memory from infancy onward, constituting the complete treasury from which regeneration draws its material.
entries.notes: Ten firmaments, ten vehicles of Jesus, ten works of the Ambassador, ten parts (five male, five female) — ten signifies the complete fullness of what constitutes the structural basis of the spiritual world. The ten firmaments are the ten ascending degrees of heavenly consciousness.

entries.spiritual_meaning: All things of faith and the church in their completeness — the full complement of truths and goods that constitute a complete spiritual order
entries.opposite_sense: When belonging to darkness: a counterfeit completeness of falsity — the full system of evil organized to oppose the Divine
entries.definition: Twelve signifies all things of faith and love in their completeness — the full and total complement of goods and truths that together constitute a complete spiritual order, whether heavenly or infernal.
entries.notes: Twelve hours of each day and night, twelve judges, twelve zodiacal signs, twelve seals, twelve spirits of error, twelve wisdoms — twelve always signifies completeness of an organized spiritual system. The twelve signs of the zodiac when inverted become the twelve governing principles of evil's dominion.

entries.spiritual_meaning: Complete dominion as to both good and truth — the fullness of spiritual governance through the conjunction of derivative goods and derivative truths
entries.opposite_sense: When belonging to darkness: fourteen heads of the dragon = complete perversion of governance over both will and understanding
entries.definition: As 7+7 or as 5+5+2+2, fourteen signifies the complete dominion that arises from the conjunction of goods and truths in their holy fullness — both the seven of celestial completeness and its mirror in the spiritual degree, united.
entries.notes: The fourteen aeons of light are explicitly enumerated as 5+5+2+2 (five sons of the First Man, five sons of the Living Spirit, plus the summons and obedience). The fourteen heads of the dragon similarly comprise seven sense-faculties above and seven below — a complete perversion of governance.

entries.spiritual_meaning: The fullness of governing principles across all degrees — complete spiritual governance as it operates through every plane of existence
entries.definition: As 9+9, eighteen signifies the fullness of governing authority distributed between the interior heavens and the exterior spiritual world — nine governing principles in each realm, together constituting the complete system of divine governance.
entries.notes: Eighteen thrones (9 in the outer aeons + 9 in the zone) and eighteen garments surrounding a child (9 + 9) — in both cases signifying the complete covering or governance of spiritual reality from both the interior and exterior sides.

entries.spiritual_meaning: Fullness of manifestation multiplied by itself — the complete self-replication of all five faculties within each of the five faculties
entries.definition: As 5×5, twenty-five signifies the complete interpenetration of the five spiritual faculties — each faculty containing within itself the full complement of all five, producing a total integration of manifestation at every level.
entries.notes: The twenty-five characteristics 'in their twenty-five limbs' explicitly derive from five times five — each of the five garments of the First Man containing five interior powers. This signifies total integration: every faculty of spiritual perception contains within itself the complete structure of all five.

entries.spiritual_meaning: The collecting of scattered goods and truths into spiritual unity — the progressive reintegration of what had been dispersed through the fall
entries.definition: As the act of collecting scattered things into one place, gathering corresponds to the spiritual process of reintegrating dispersed goods and truths — bringing back into unity what had been scattered through the fall into falsity and evil.
entries.notes: The Light Mind is called 'the gatherer in of the ones who are scattered' — Divine Wisdom's essential function is to collect all dispersed affections and truths back into the unity of the regenerate will.

entries.spiritual_meaning: Interior truth in its seminal state — truth implanted in the mind that has the potential to grow into understanding and produce good works
entries.definition: As the germ from which a plant grows, a seed corresponds to an interior truth in its earliest state — truth implanted by the Lord in the understanding that contains within itself the potential for growth into full comprehension and the production of charitable works.
entries.notes: Seeds that are 'threshed, plucked, and cut down' correspond to interior truths that are violated and consumed by the proprium before they can mature.

entries.spiritual_meaning: The craving for conjunction of evil with falsity — the quality of desire that binds falsity to evil love
entries.definition: As a substance that creates thirst and preserves through desiccation, salt corresponds to the craving or desire quality by which evil seeks conjunction with falsity — the preservative force that maintains the bond between corrupt will and corrupt understanding.
entries.notes: The salty inner sea signifies natural knowledge corrupted by the residue of evil — the lingering taste of bitterness from the washing-out of corrupted truth.

entries.spiritual_meaning: Interior torment — the grief and anguish of unmixed evil; spiritual suffering
entries.definition: As a taste that causes involuntary rejection and pain, bitterness corresponds to interior spiritual torment — the inherent suffering that constitutes the very life of evil when it is stripped of all stolen goods and exposed in its true nature.
entries.notes: Bitterness as the taste of the world of Darkness and as the fourth property of the King of Darkness ('his own soul') teaches that the essential life of evil is torment — evil's own experience of itself is bitter.

entries.spiritual_meaning: Deceptive delight of falsified truth — the seductive quality that makes falsity appear desirable
entries.opposite_sense: In positive sense: genuine spiritual delight
entries.definition: As the most attractive taste, sweetness corresponds to delight — in the negative sense, the deceptive pleasantness by which falsified truth seduces the understanding into accepting what is false; in the positive sense, the genuine delight that accompanies truth from good.
entries.notes: The 'sweetness of water' as the taste of the water-world (perverted truth) teaches that falsified truth is especially dangerous because it tastes pleasant — seducing the understanding through false delight.

entries.spiritual_meaning: The lust for dominion from self-love — the predatory quality of the ruling love of self that seeks to devour and control all others
entries.definition: As the predatory animal associated with the pride of dominion over all other beasts, the lion corresponds to the lust for dominion from self-love — the quality of the ruling self that seeks to exert supreme power over all things.
entries.notes: The lion-face of the King of Darkness's head and the king of the fire-world teaches that the love of dominion is the highest quality of evil — the 'head' of all infernal organization.

entries.spiritual_meaning: Predatory rationality — intellectual power turned to self-serving ends; the capacity to see from above in order to seize
entries.definition: As the bird that sees from great heights and swoops down to seize prey, the eagle corresponds to predatory rationality — the intellectual faculty when it serves self-love, using its elevated perspective not to illuminate but to identify and capture what it desires.
entries.notes: The eagle-face of the King of Darkness's shoulders and the wind-world king teaches that false reasoning occupies the 'shoulders' of evil — the power and capacity that evil uses to elevate itself and attack from above.

entries.spiritual_meaning: The falsification of all truth — the comprehensive distortion of understanding that perverts every true perception into its opposite
entries.definition: As the mythological beast that combines predatory qualities with deception, the dragon corresponds to the falsification of all truth — the comprehensive corruption of the understanding that twists every genuine perception into a counterfeit serving evil ends.
entries.notes: The dragon with fourteen heads described in the final chapters is explicitly equated with 'the thought of the body' — self-derived thinking in all its organized complexity, with seven perceptive faculties above and seven below.

entries.spiritual_meaning: Base corporeal knowing — the lowest form of natural knowledge perverted to infernal ends
entries.opposite_sense: In positive sense: natural knowledge seized from the waters of the external mind
entries.definition: As the creature that lives in the depths of water and cannot rise above it, the fish corresponds to the most sensory and corporeal form of knowing — natural knowledge that remains at the lowest level and, when perverted, serves only the basest purposes.
entries.notes: The fish-face of the King of Darkness's tail corresponds to the most external expression of evil — the ultimates of sensory cunning. Being caught 'like fish in the sea' signifies natural knowledges seized from the mass of sensory knowledge.

entries.spiritual_meaning: Endless revolving from one false appearance into another — the condition of spiritual vastation in which the soul cycles through successive states without rest
entries.definition: As the passage of a soul through body after body without finding rest, transmigration corresponds to the spiritual condition of endless vastation — the perpetual cycling through successive false states that characterizes the intermediate condition of those not yet confirmed in either good or evil.
entries.notes: Transmigration is presented as one of the eight 'mixed' paths — neither pure ascent nor pure descent, but the intermediate condition of those whose spiritual state is not yet determined.

entries.spiritual_meaning: Concupiscence — disordered desire proceeding from self-love; the active force of the proprium that seeks to possess and consume what belongs to the Divine
entries.definition: As intense, consuming desire for possession, lust corresponds to concupiscence — the active force of the self-derived will that seeks to possess, consume, and appropriate everything to itself, especially what belongs to the Divine.
entries.notes: Lust is consistently paired with fire as 'the father and mother' of all evil — self-love (fire) and concupiscence (lust) together generate all derivative evil. This directly parallels Swedenborg's teaching that the love of self and the love of the world are the two universal origins of all evil.

entries.spiritual_meaning: The perception of spiritual delight — the sphere of good perceived through interior sense; the quality of celestial acknowledgment
entries.opposite_sense: When foul: spiritual putrefaction and corruption
entries.definition: As the subtle quality perceived through the sense of smell, perfume corresponds to the sphere of spiritual good as perceived through interior sensation — the delight of love perceived not through the understanding but through the affectional plane.
entries.notes: The Father's 'sweet perfume' that 'takes away all affliction' corresponds to the sphere of divine good that, when perceived, removes all spiritual suffering. The 'stench' of evil is its opposite — the sphere of corruption that emanates from hell.

entries.spiritual_meaning: The highest governing wisdom — supreme truth that crowns and rules the whole spiritual life
entries.definition: As the ornament placed upon the head signifying supreme authority, a crown corresponds to the highest wisdom — the governing truth that presides over the whole of the spiritual life and signifies authority derived from the Divine.
entries.notes: Three types are distinguished: diadem (highest wisdom), wreath (intelligence), crown (illuminated knowledge) — corresponding to three degrees of truth that govern the regenerate mind.

entries.spiritual_meaning: The conjunction of interior affections — the intimate union of love with truth, or of one good with another
entries.definition: As the expression of intimate affection between persons, the kiss corresponds to the conjunction of interior affections — the spiritual union of love with truth, or of one celestial good with another, in which the inmost qualities of each are communicated.
entries.notes: One of the five mysteries of the First Man — five modes of spiritual conjunction. The kiss signifies the deepest mode of affectional union, distinct from the peace (conjunction of good), the right hand (communication of power), the salutation (humble acknowledgment), and the laying on of hands (transmission of authority).

entries.spiritual_meaning: The transmission of interior spiritual authority — the communication of governing power from a higher to a lower degree
entries.definition: As the ritual gesture of conferring authority or blessing, the laying on of hands corresponds to the transmission of interior spiritual authority — the communication of governing power from a celestial good to its derivative, enabling the lower to act with the authority of the higher.
entries.notes: The second laying on of hands — given after the First Man's victory — enables him to 'become leader of his brethren in the new aeon,' teaching that authority to govern in the regenerated state is conferred only after the completion of temptation-combat.

entries.spiritual_meaning: Thought — a swift act of spiritual perception; rational thought that rises freely through the atmosphere of the mind
entries.definition: As a creature that moves freely through the air, a bird corresponds to thought — the rational faculty that rises through the spiritual atmosphere, moving freely between states of perception. A bird with its feathers plucked represents thought stripped of its truths.
entries.notes: A person whose Light Mind departs becomes 'as if a bird were its feathers plucked' — thought stripped of truth becomes merely natural. The bird's path through the air leaving no trace corresponds to how rational thought passes through the spiritual atmosphere without disrupting the channels of influx.

entries.spiritual_meaning: The Divine Wisdom that organizes understanding into coherent form — the power of divine ordering that constructs the interior architecture of the regenerating mind
entries.definition: As the master architect who constructs buildings according to plan, the Great Builder corresponds to the ordering power of Divine Wisdom — the capacity to organize scattered truths and goods into a coherent, functional spiritual structure that can serve as a dwelling for the Divine.
entries.notes: The Builder constructs both the 'new aeon of joy' (= new heaven) and 'a prison for the enemy' — teaching that the same ordering wisdom that builds heaven also constructs the permanent containment of hell.

entries.spiritual_meaning: An origin of truth — a living source from which understanding flows forth
entries.definition: As a natural source from which water flows forth continuously, a spring corresponds to an origin of truth — a living interior source from which understanding and doctrine flow outward to nourish the mind.
entries.notes: Springs that are 'obstructed' in the three earths correspond to the impediment of truth-sources within the natural mind that must be cleared for regeneration to proceed.

entries.spiritual_meaning: A pathway of spiritual influx — the channel through which divine life flows between interior and exterior degrees of the mind
entries.definition: As a channel that conducts fluid between locations, a conduit corresponds to a pathway of spiritual influx — the living connection through which good and truth flow between the celestial, spiritual, and natural degrees of the mind, and through which evil is also discharged downward.
entries.notes: Three conduits connect the entirety of the zone from abyss to heights — corresponding to three pathways of influx linking the lowest natural to the highest celestial. The teaching that conduits cannot be 'cut' because they are spiritual corresponds to the doctrine that influx is self-healing and cannot be permanently disrupted.

entries.spiritual_meaning: The Divine Good made manifest through wisdom — the union of love and truth as perceived by all illuminated faculties
entries.definition: As the beloved one who is honored among all the lights, this figure corresponds to the Divine Good united with wisdom — the quality of love as it is perceived and cherished by all faculties of spiritual intelligence.
entries.notes: Associated with the Great Builder and the Living Spirit as part of the third greatness. Represents the affectional dimension of the Lord's operation — what is loved and honored among all who perceive truth.

entries.spiritual_meaning: The intermediate sphere between good and evil — the boundary between the spiritual and the natural; the world of spirits
entries.definition: As the intermediate region between the upper and lower worlds, the zone corresponds to the boundary between interior and exterior states of the mind — the intermediate spiritual realm where good and evil are still mixed and where the processes of separation and judgment operate.
entries.notes: The zone is the realm where all active governance takes place — where the five watches operate, where the Light Mind enters the body, and where the paths of ascent and descent are established. It corresponds to the world of spirits between heaven and hell.

summary.consistency_assessment: The spiritual readings produced per-chapter show high convergence for the major cosmological entities: the Father of Greatness as Divine Love, the First Man as the Celestial Human descending into temptation, the Living Spirit as proceeding Divine Truth, and darkness as falsity from evil are virtually unanimous throughout. Moderate divergence appears in the rendering of 'fire' (sometimes 'love,' sometimes 'self-love' — resolved by recognizing the dual sense), 'water' (sometimes 'truth,' sometimes 'falsity' — resolved by the living/dark distinction), and especially the Ambassador (sometimes 'Divine Providence,' sometimes 'mediating Divine Truth' — resolved by recognizing providence as one function of the Ambassador's broader mediating role). The greatest systematic divergence concerns numbers: the per-chapter readings frequently treated numbers literally rather than correspondentially, especially five (usually rendered as 'five faculties' without recognizing the correspondential weight of fiveness itself) and twelve (often treated as a count rather than as signifying completeness). The lexicon addresses this by giving each significant number its own entry. Random divergence appears in the rendering of lesser figures (e.g. the Keeper of Splendour, the King of Glory) where chapter-level context sometimes overspecified the spiritual function.
summary.five_fold_systems: The text's architecture is built upon interlocking systems of five. The primary system is the five elements (fire, light, water, wind, air) which map to five spiritual faculties (love, wisdom, truth, understanding, perception). These appear across multiple planes: (1) Five garments of the First Man = five external truths; (2) Five sons of the First Man = five faculties of celestial perception; (3) Five sons of the Living Spirit = five structural powers sustaining spiritual order; (4) Five dark elements (smoke, fire, wind, water, darkness) = five genera of evil; (5) Five limbs of the good tree (consideration, counsel, insight, thought, mind) = five ascending faculties from outermost reception to inmost willing; (6) Five limbs of the bad tree = the same five faculties inverted; (7) Five fathers proceeding one from another = five discrete degrees of divine influx; (8) Five senses of the body = five perceptive faculties. All these fives interlock: the five garments clothe the five sons who correspond to the five elements which in turn map onto the five senses and the five limbs. The number five thus signifies the complete manifestation of any spiritual reality at a given level. The secondary system is the three (three earths, three vessels, three garments, three emanations from each father) signifying discrete degrees — celestial, spiritual, natural — which intersect the fivefold system to produce the text's full architecture. The twelve (= 4×3 or 5+5+2) system unifies the spatial (four quarters) with the vertical (three degrees) or the manifest (five) with the communicative (two = summons and obedience).
summary.key_findings:
1. THE FIVEFOLD ARCHITECTURE IS FUNDAMENTAL: Five is not merely frequent but constitutive — the entire cosmos in this text is organized in fives at every level, from the Divine itself (five limbs of the Father) to the human body (five senses). No comparable Zoroastrian or Manichaean source uses five with this systematic precision, suggesting an underlying doctrine of correspondence rather than arbitrary cosmological numbering.

2. MATTER AS ACTIVE PROPRIUM: The identification of 'Matter' (Gk. hyle) not with inert substance but with 'the thought of death' — an active fashioning intelligence — maps precisely to Swedenborg's proprium (the self-derived will that creates all evil forms). This is not a passive principle but a sculptor.

3. THE THREE DISCHARGES = SWEDENBORG'S ORDER OF VASTATION: The sequence in which the three vessels are expelled — first corrupted truth (water), then spiritual blindness (darkness), then self-love (fire) — matches exactly Swedenborg's teaching that falsities of the understanding are addressed before evils of the will in regeneration, with self-love being the deepest and last to be removed.

4. THE SUMMONS/OBEDIENCE PAIR AS INFLUX AND RECEPTION: These two figures, consistently paired throughout, correspond to the two fundamental movements of all spiritual communication: the Lord's active proceeding (summons) and the human will's free response (obedience). Their being called 'father and mother' teaches that all spiritual generation requires both.

5. VIRGINAL vs. CONTINENT = CELESTIAL vs. SPIRITUAL INNOCENCE: The text's explicit distinction between wisdom that was never defiled ('virginal') and wisdom purified after defilement ('continent') maps precisely onto Swedenborg's distinction between celestial innocence and spiritual innocence.

6. THE WHEEL'S AUTHORITY THROUGH THE FALL: The teaching that the cycle of natural knowledges gained authority over perception and the proprium only because evil fell upon it during the Ambassador's manifestation corresponds to the doctrine that natural knowledge has no inherent spiritual power — it became master over human fate only through the fall, not through legitimate divine ordering.

7. EVIL'S SELF-CONTRADICTION AS ITS DESTRUCTION: The text explicitly states that evil was 'destined to perish because of the disunity present in all of them,' while wisdom endures because 'no disunity or discord exists in the light.' This is one of the clearest statements in ancient literature of the self-destroying nature of evil.
